Exercise A

Simple, continuous or perfect?

Use the past perfect (had + past participle) for something that happened before another point in the story, the past continuous for an action in progress, and the past simple for the main events. Choose the correct form for each gap.

Before you start — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking. You can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Six moments from a busy week

1. When we got to the library, all the desks 1 (go).

2. By the time I started university, I 2 (already / study) English for eight years.

3. While I 3 (wait) for the bus, I 4 (realise) that I 5 (leave) my laptop at home.

4. By the time the lecturer 6 (arrive), we 7 (finish) our slide.

5. She 8 (feel) nervous because she 9 (not / prepare) her notes.

6. What 10 (you / do) when the fire alarm 11 (go) off?

Exercise B

Plan your story

In a moment you will tell a partner a two-minute story from your life: a trip that went wrong, a great first day, or a time you got lost. Write short notes for each part. You will speak from these notes, not from a script.

Exercise C

Write your story

You have told your story to a partner. Now write it for your teacher in 120–150 words. Use all three past tenses, and add one detail your partner asked about.

Word count: 0 (aim for 120–150)
